name: coordination/dispatch-envelope
description:
The coordination dispatch envelope (ADR-0016 §2, `spec/ext/coord-dispatch.v1.schema.json`) — what actually goes on the wire when a consented dispatch is carried to its pinned recipient. It is deliberately NOT a contract: no objective, no deliverable, no deadline, no capability request, because the risk card the operator read named none of those and akson's contract schema could only carry this payload by inventing them. Every member is either something the operator consented to (the payload by its digest, the recipient, the task type, the staged digest, the consent receipt) or something the receiver needs in order to check that fact (the two roots, the protocol, the schema version).

The two verifications this vector freezes, both re-derivable from these bytes alone: SHA-256 over the payload must equal `payload_sha256`, and the ADR-0016 §4 derivation over {payload_sha256, recipient_label, task_type} must reproduce `staged_digest` — which is why `recipient_label` is on the wire at all. The envelope is carried as a Part of media type `application/vnd.akson-dev.coord-dispatch.v1+json` beside the raw payload Part, with the dispatch receipt as the A2A Message id so a sender's recovery retry deduplicates at the recipient. It is NOT signed: its authenticity is the pinned mutual-TLS channel's, and there is no key purpose for a coordination dispatch.
